question: Unlike hospital nursing which looks after one patient at a time, what is the main focus of community health nursing?

options.A: The health of entire populations and communities
options.B: Critical care management in intensive units

explanation: Spot on! While hospital nurses care for individual bedside patients, community nurses look at the bigger picture—the health needs of whole neighborhoods and populations.

question: Why is community health nursing so important to primary health care in Nigeria?

options.A: It manages all tertiary hospital admissions across the country
options.B: It brings preventative and basic health services directly to local populations
options.C: It exclusively handles complex surgical procedures in rural areas
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors in government hospitals

explanation: You got it! By stepping into local clinics, schools, and homes, community health nurses make sure everyday preventative care actually reaches where people live.

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

options.A: Only the head of the household
options.C: Patients admitted to the surgical ward

explanation: Exactly! The heart of public health nursing is treating the whole community—not just one person—as your main patient.

question: When planning a new health program in a village, why is it vital for a nurse to involve local leaders?

options.A: To shift all financial responsibility onto the community members
options.B: To replace the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: To comply with international travel regulations
options.D: To ensure the program respects local values and gains community acceptance

explanation: Well done! Working with local leaders builds trust and makes sure your health projects fit nicely with the culture and lifestyle of the people.

question: Which of these is a classic example of stopping a disease before it even starts (primary prevention)?

options.B: Screening adults for high blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention stops illnesses before they happen. Vaccines are the ultimate example of keeping trouble away before it starts.

question: A nurse sets up a desk in the village square to check blood sugar levels for healthy adults. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: You nailed it! Screening tests catch health issues early before big symptoms show up, which is what secondary prevention is all about.

question: What is the main goal of striving for health equity in our communities?

options.A: Eliminating all private hospitals in the healthcare sector
options.B: Ensuring equal funding for all urban medical centers
options.C: Ensuring everyone has a fair opportunity to achieve good health
options.D: Providing identical medical treatments to every single person

explanation: Exactly right! Health equity means clearing away unfair barriers so that everyone, no matter their background, has a fair shot at being healthy.

question: Why do we often view rural villagers and urban slum residents as vulnerable populations?

options.A: They possess unlimited financial resources for private clinics
options.B: They always reject traditional and modern medical treatments equally
options.C: They have complete immunity against all infectious diseases
options.D: They face severe barriers to accessing affordable and quality healthcare services

explanation: Spot on! Distance, poverty, and a lack of nearby clinics make it really tough for these groups to get the standard care they deserve.

question: In simple terms, what does epidemiology study?

options.A: The distribution and determinants of diseases in populations
options.B: The microscopic structure of human body tissues
options.C: The chemical composition of pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: The financial management of healthcare institutions

explanation: You got it! Epidemiology is basically disease detective work—it figures out who is getting sick, why it's happening, and how sickness spreads.

question: Why is it so crucial for a community nurse to track and report disease numbers quickly?

options.A: It prevents patients from visiting traditional healers
options.B: It guarantees immediate promotion within the nursing profession
options.C: It allows for early detection and rapid containment of disease outbreaks
options.D: It removes the need for community health education programs

explanation: Well done! Catching an unusual spike in illnesses early helps public health teams jump in and stop an outbreak before it goes wild.

question: What is the main purpose of community empowerment in public health?

options.A: Forcing citizens to obey strict government health laws
options.B: Generating revenue for local health insurance schemes
options.C: Enabling people to take charge of their own health and environment
options.D: Reducing the workload of doctors in tertiary hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Empowerment is about giving everyday people the tools and confidence to solve their own health problems in a lasting way.

question: Why should community nurses use simple everyday language and live demonstrations during health talks?

options.A: To discourage people from asking questions during lectures
options.B: To ensure clear understanding and encourage practical application by listeners
options.C: To make the teaching session take as little time as possible
options.D: To hide complex medical terminology from uneducated citizens

explanation: Exactly! Keeping it simple ensures everyone follows along and can actually practice what they learned when they go home.

question: Who are typical members of an interdisciplinary community health team?

options.A: Environmental health officers, social workers, and nurses
options.B: Surgeons, pharmacists, and medical equipment vendors
options.C: Private legal practitioners and financial auditors
options.D: Only registered nurses and hospital administrators

explanation: You got it! Community health brings together different experts like nurses, social workers, and environmental officers to tackle all angles of wellness.

question: Why do community nurses need to collaborate with other professionals when solving health problems?

options.A: It reduces the cost of running primary healthcare clinics
options.B: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without community input
options.C: Complex health problems require diverse skills and coordinated efforts
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to conduct home visits

explanation: Spot on! Because health is tied to housing, water, and social life, different professionals have to team up to find real solutions.

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system does community health nursing support the most?
explanation: You nailed it! Community health nurses work right at the grassroots level, which is the solid foundation of primary health care in Nigeria.

question: How does great community health nursing help ease the burden on big tertiary hospitals in Nigeria?

options.A: By restricting patient movement from rural areas into big cities
options.B: By preventing and treating illnesses early at the local level before they become severe
options.C: By turning primary health centers into major surgical teaching hospitals
options.D: By replacing doctors with nurses in emergency rooms nationwide

explanation: Fantastic! Catching and treating issues early in the neighborhood keeps patients healthy and keeps those big tertiary hospitals from getting too crowded.
